shared_elements: T-shaped / broad-topped monolithic stone pillar with shoulder-like lateral projections
low-relief carving on a rough stone surface
quadruped animal in profile with head and legs indicated
elongated narrow vertical motifs (rod- or limb-like elements) flanking the field
horizontal division of the surface into an upper cap/head zone and a lower body zone
small subsidiary figures set within the larger field
justification: Both are T-shaped stone monoliths whose broad upper block carries carving and whose shaft below bears a profile quadruped surrounded by narrow vertical rod-like elements, a fairly specific compositional scheme rather than a generic coincidence. The clearest difference is legibility and finish: A's reliefs are crisply cut, deeply modelled and organised into distinct horizontal registers including a banded zigzag frieze and a large bird, whereas B's carvings are shallow, weathered and ambiguous, with no clear register band and a coarser, darker stone.
